label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "It makes me feel frightened, girls. Do you suppose it’s really right to act like this? Mrs. Lynde says that all play-acting is abominably wicked."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I’ll try. I’ll think over what you have said, and try to believe it. And you’ll come up as often as you can, won’t you, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "There’s a concert at Carmody and a party at White Sands. Herb Spencer’s going to take me. He’s my latest. Be sure to come up tomorrow. I’m dying for a good talk with you. I want to hear all about your doings at Redmond."

label: History
value: Rusty was found thin.
unit: After being found thin, singed, and damaged, Rusty trotted close to Anne's heels as he followed her home, having recently fought and defeated the tobacco-king's cat. Anne reluctantly adopted the disreputable stray at Patty's Place, where he miraculously survived a chloroforming attempt and earned a permanent spot in the house. Upon Aunt Jamesina's arrival with her own pets, Rusty attempted to fight the newcomers, getting put in his place by the Sarah-cat while engaging in repeated battles with Joseph before eventually becoming his close friend. He later contributed to a chaotic scene at Patty's Place when Royal Gardner's mother and sisters made an unexpected visit.

label: History
value: Miss Sarah Copp lived at her house on the Tory Road.
unit: Miss Sarah Copp lived at her house on the Tory Road with her sister Martha, who forced her to whitewash an old duck house every spring. Twenty years prior, Sarah had wanted to marry Luther Wallace, but her father sent him away because he was poor. Anne Shirley later fell through the roof of this duck house while trying to look for a willow-ware platter, leading Sarah to rescue her, invite her inside for tea, sell her the platter, and announce that she was finally getting married. Separately, a cat given to Aunt Jamesina by her washerwoman was named the Sarah-cat, who eventually moved into Patty's Place and promptly put a stray cat named Rusty in his place.

label: History
value: Stacy served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea.
unit: Miss Stacy served as the schoolteacher in Avonlea, maintaining order without ever whipping her pupils. Upon starting her tenure, she proposed organizing a Christmas concert to raise funds for a school flag, which her students eagerly embraced. At the end of her first term, she announced she would return the following year to prepare students for the Queen's Entrance examination, subsequently guiding them through their studies for the crucial tests. She eventually left Avonlea after accepting a position at a grade school in her home district.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant before spending time working as a schoolteacher. Looking ahead to her next year of college, she proposed renting a house with Anne and Priscilla, suggesting her Aunt Jamesina act as their housekeeper. The group, joined by Philippa Gordon, successfully secured Patty's Place and settled into a lively household together for the school year. During their time living at Patty's Place, Stella and her housemates balanced their Redmond examinations with household antics, social calls, and creative endeavors, including a rainy afternoon spent with Anne reading old melodramatic stories. As their college life drew to a close after graduation, Stella packed up her belongings alongside her friends as they prepared to part ways.

label: Personality
value: Susan is a grim-faced handmaiden.
unit: Susan is a grim-faced, gray, and gaunt handmaiden of the Blythe family at Ingleside, known for being faithful, kind-hearted, and practical. Characterized as an elderly spinster, she holds a deep respect for the clergy and enjoys discussing funerals. She approaches life with a calm pragmatism, serenely doing what she can for humanity's betterment while leaving the rest to Higher Powers rather than trying to run the world. Unsentimental about literature, she views poetry as mostly composed of lies, though she insists on maintaining tradition by serving pudding on Sundays. Skilled at knitting, she harbors a constant fear that the children will poison themselves by eating roots gathered near the pond, and she intends to visit to view Rosemary's trousseau.

label: History
value: Susan Baker is an unmarried woman
unit: Susan Baker, an un married woman who never had a beau, once had an uncle who began as a poet and ended up becoming a tramp. She returned from caring for a sick neighbor to work as hired help for Anne and Gilbert, making an unconscious funny remark that sent Gilbert and Captain Jim outside laughing. Following the tragic loss of Anne's firstborn, Gilbert and Susan insisted that Anne keep Susan on as help for the summer so she could regain her health. Over the following years, Susan remained an integral part of the household, helping nurse Anne back to health after she gave birth to a healthy baby boy named James Matthew. After Susan's sister broke her leg, Susan temporarily left Four Winds to tend to her, returning late from the Glen with local news and expressing surprise at Miss Cornelia's impending marriage. When Anne and Gilbert later relocated their growing family from the house of dreams to the Glen, Susan moved with them to Ingleside. At Ingleside, Susan regularly conversed with Anne and Miss Cornelia, sharing local gossip while helping care for Anne's younger children, Rilla and baby Shirley. When the Meredith children sprinted to Ingleside terrified after mistaking a neighbor for a ghost, Susan soothed them and investigated the garden dyke armed with a pitchfork, later returning to reveal the embarrassing truth. She remained a steadfast presence at Ingleside, frequently discussing parish rumors, local scandals, and upcoming weddings with Anne and Miss Cornelia.

unit: Susan Baker, an un married woman who never had a beau, once had an uncle who began as a poet and ended up becoming a tramp. She returned from caring for a sick neighbor to work as hired help for Anne and Gilbert, making an unconscious funny remark that sent Gilbert and Captain Jim outside laughing. Following the tragic loss of Anne's firstborn, Gilbert and Susan insisted that Anne keep Susan on as help for the summer so she could regain her health. Over the following years, Susan remained an integral part of the household, helping nurse Anne back to health after she gave birth to a healthy baby boy named James Matthew. After Susan's sister broke her leg, Susan temporarily left Four Winds to tend to her, returning late from the Glen with local news and expressing surprise at Miss Cornelia's impending marriage. When Anne and Gilbert later relocated their growing family from the house of dreams to the Glen, Susan moved with them to Ingleside. At Ingleside, Susan regularly conversed with Anne and Miss Cornelia, sharing local gossip while helping care for Anne's younger children, Rilla and baby Shirley. When the Meredith children sprinted to Ingleside terrified after mistaking a neighbor for a ghost, Susan soothed them and investigated the garden dyke armed with a pitchfork, later returning to reveal the embarrassing truth. She remained a steadfast presence at Ingleside, frequently discussing parish rumors, local scandals, and upcoming weddings with Anne and Miss Cornelia.

value: Una is sweet.
unit: Una is a sweet, dreamy, and sensitive young girl who dislikes fighting and possesses a deep capacity for sympathy toward others. Extremely shy, she finds asking favors of anyone to be an agony, yet she remains acutely sensitive to public opinion. Though not prone to much laughter, she truly enjoys praying, and her hidden life is driven by the quiet dream of taking music lessons.

label: History
value: Una Meredith lived in Maywater before coming to Glen St. Mary
unit: Before coming to Glen St. Mary, Una Meredith lived in Maywater and lost her mother when she was six years old. At ten years old, she settled into the manse with her family and quickly formed a close friendship with the neighbouring Blythe children in Rainbow Valley. After discovering a starved runaway named Mary Vance hiding in a barn, Una comforted the girl through the night and later plucked up the courage to beg Miss Cornelia to adopt Mary so she would not be sent back to an asylum. During a week when Aunt Martha fell ill, Una and Faith attempted to run the household, inadvertently creating a local scandal by shaking rugs in the graveyard on what neighbors mistook for Sunday. As community gossip and criticism surrounding their father mounted, Una helped establish the Good-Conduct Club with her siblings to discipline themselves and protect their father's reputation. After a self-imposed daylong fast caused Una to faint during a church service, their father resolved to be more attentive. Fearing the idea of a stepmother due to Mary Vance's stories, Una felt self-conscious about her shabby clothes and worried about local rumors regarding her father's love life. However, upon witnessing her father's deep anguish in his study, Una selflessly visited Rosemary West to beg her to marry him, promising that the children would be good. Rosemary agreed to write to her father, and Una later celebrated with her family in Rainbow Valley on the eve of the upcoming double wedding.

unit: Before coming to Glen St. Mary, Una Meredith lived in Maywater and lost her mother when she was six years old. At ten years old, she settled into the manse with her family and quickly formed a close friendship with the neighbouring Blythe children in Rainbow Valley. After discovering a starved runaway named Mary Vance hiding in a barn, Una comforted the girl through the night and later plucked up the courage to beg Miss Cornelia to adopt Mary so she would not be sent back to an asylum. During a week when Aunt Martha fell ill, Una and Faith attempted to run the household, inadvertently creating a local scandal by shaking rugs in the graveyard on what neighbors mistook for Sunday. As community gossip and criticism surrounding their father mounted, Una helped establish the Good-Conduct Club with her siblings to discipline themselves and protect their father's reputation. After a self-imposed daylong fast caused Una to faint during a church service, their father resolved to be more attentive. Fearing the idea of a stepmother due to Mary Vance's stories, Una felt self-conscious about her shabby clothes and worried about local rumors regarding her father's love life. However, upon witnessing her father's deep anguish in his study, Una selflessly visited Rosemary West to beg her to marry him, promising that the children would be good. Rosemary agreed to write to her father, and Una later celebrated with her family in Rainbow Valley on the eve of the upcoming double wedding.

label: Quote
value: Una Meredith said: "I don’t believe God will send you to hell for telling lies when you didn’t know it was wrong. He couldn’t. Why, He’s kind and good. Of course, you mustn’t tell any more now that you know it’s wrong."

label: Quote
value: Una Meredith said: "Aunt Martha never makes any. But Miss Susan at Ingleside does, and sometimes she lets us have a plateful in Rainbow Valley. Do you know what I do when I’m hungry for doughnuts and can’t get any, Mrs. Elliott?"

label: Quote
value: Una Meredith said: "But God put it into her heart to take you. All my putting it into her head wouldn’t have done any good if He hadn’t."

label: Quote
value: Una Meredith said: "Oh, no, no, Mary. I’m sure it couldn’t be right to pray to the devil. And it wouldn’t do any good because he’s bad. It might aggravate him and he’d be worse than ever."

label: Quote
value: Una Meredith said: "It’s just being a stepmother changes them. Mary says they can’t help it. I wouldn’t mind the whippings so much as having father hate us."

label: History
value: Uncle Jim was born into a family of sea-going people.
unit: Born into a family of sea-going people, Uncle Jim ran off to sea as a boy and spent most of his life sailing the world. Over fifty years ago, he lost his sweetheart Margaret when she drifted away in a dory, and he searched for her body along the shore for months. Throughout his adventurous travels, he gathered stories and material, eventually settling down at Four Winds Harbor to tend the lighthouse five years prior to meeting Anne and Gilbert Blythe. Recognizing Anne as a kindred spirit, he welcomed the couple into his life, sharing his collection of curios, entertaining them with sea tales, and introducing them to his orange cat, First Mate. In time, he entrusted his cherished journal of sea adventures to Anne and Gilbert, hoping his life story might one day be written down. Following the tragic loss of Anne's first child, he offered her comfort by sharing the history of his lost love Margaret and asking Anne to keep her memory alive. When writer Owen Ford visited Four Winds, Uncle Jim allowed him to borrow his life-book and collaborate on a manuscript weaving his sea experiences with Margaret's story. Later, Uncle Jim financially assisted Leslie Moore when she needed to travel to Montreal, and he was honored when Anne and Gilbert named their newborn son James Matthew after him. Aware of his impending death, he entrusted the care of First Mate to Anne shortly before bestowing a warm benediction upon Leslie and Owen when they announced their love. Upon receiving a published copy of his completed life-book from Anne and Leslie, Uncle Jim peacefully passed away in his sleep at the lighthouse with the book resting on his chest.

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "Come, now, Cornelia, I can’t see any harm in going to the Methodist church when there’s no preaching in your own. I’ve been a Presbyterian for seventy-six years, and it isn’t likely my theology will hoist anchor at this late day."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "I wanted to hear some good singing. The Methodists have a good choir; and you can’t deny, Cornelia, that the singing in our church is awful since the split in the choir."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "That’s just exactly the truth about Lewis Taylor. When I see those poor, miserable children of his, robbed of all children ought to have, it p’isens my own bite and sup for days afterwards."

label: Quote
value: Walter said: "The flower angel’s aren’t. They are a pale misty blue, just like the haze in the valley. Oh, how I wish I could fly. It must be glorious."

label: Quote
value: Walter said: “I never fought before—and I didn’t want to right up to the last—and then,” said Walter, determined to make a clean breast of it, “I liked it while I was at it.”

label: Quote
value: Walter said: "But I’m not going to be frightened any more, sir. Being frightened of things is worse than the things themselves. I’m going to ask father to take me over to Lowbridge to-morrow to get my tooth out."

label: Quote
value: Walter said: "It would be a big pain. I hate being hurt. Father said he wouldn’t insist on my going—he’d wait until I’d made up my own mind to go."

label: Quote
value: Walter said: "I didn’t say I would run. I said I wanted to run. That’s a different thing. I want to help people, too. But oh, I wish there weren’t any ugly, dreadful things in the world. I wish everything was glad and beautiful."

unit: Anne adjusts to life at Queen's Academy, forming close friendships with Stella and Priscilla while continuing her intense academic rivalry with Gilbert. She enjoys weekend visits home to Avonlea during the autumn and spends spare time visiting Miss Barry at Beechwood. As spring arrives and final exams loom, Anne and her friends gather to discuss their anxieties, upcoming commencement clothes, and hopes for the future.

value: Anne bids a tearful farewell to her home at Green Gables.
chapter: v3 · Chapter III Greeting and Farewell
unit: Anne bids a tearful farewell to her home at Green Gables and leaves for Redmond College with Gilbert and Charlie Sloane. After a rainy drive to the station and a boat ride from Charlottetown, she and Gilbert travel by train to Kingsport. Upon arrival, Anne is warmly met by Priscilla Grant, who takes her by cab to their new boardinghouse while cheering her up.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

label: v3 · Chapter VI In the Park
value: Anne goes for an afternoon walk.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VI In the Park
unit: Anne, Priscilla, and Phil Gordon go for an afternoon walk with Gilbert and Charlie Sloane through the park and along the harbor shore. After watching the sunset from a pavilion, they walk back via Spofford Avenue where Phil points out a charming, quaint house called Patty's Place. Anne feels an instant connection to the house and has a strong presentiment that she will become better acquainted with it.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

Asked by Marilla to share her true background, Anne recounts her life as an orphan, describing her parents' deaths and her childhood moving between homes and looking after children before being sent to the asylum. Listening to Anne's history, Marilla begins to feel deep pity for the neglected child and considers whether they should keep her after all.

During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

chapter: v3 · Chapter XIII The Way of Transgressors
unit: Rebelling against Mrs. Lynde's instructions, Davy convinces Dora to skip Sunday School so they can go fishing and play with the Cottons. Late that night, Davy confesses everything to Anne, who forgives him and encourages him to apologize to God.

unit: Faith causes a scandal at church by attending without stockings, which leads to gossip across the Glen and discussions among Anne, Susan, and Miss Cornelia. In Rainbow Valley, Nan and Di defend Faith when Mary Vance criticizes her, but Jerry and the Conduct Club decide to punish Faith by making her wear her hated striped stockings. To clear her father's name and clarify other misunderstandings, Faith writes and publishes a detailed letter of explanation in the local newspaper.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
value: Anne discusses her mistake with Mrs. Lynde
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: Anne discusses her mistake with Mrs. Lynde before going to Orchard Slope to take the blame directly. She bravely confronts the angry Miss Josephine Barry and explains her perspective, winning over the old lady with her sincerity and imagination. Miss Barry decides to stay in Avonlea after all, and she and Anne become firm friends.

unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. Later, Anne and Diana take a walk through the woods and accidentally lose their way while heading to a tea party. Their wrong turn leads them to Echo Lodge, where they meet the eccentric Miss Lavendar Lewis and her young maid, Charlotta the Fourth, who invite them to stay for a pretend tea party.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

value: Davy rebels against Mrs. Lynde's instructions
chapter: v3 · Chapter XIII The Way of Transgressors
unit: Rebelling against Mrs. Lynde's instructions, Davy convinces Dora to skip Sunday School so they can go fishing and play with the Cottons. Afterwards, Davy lies to Mrs. Lynde to cover up his disobedience, but he is tormented by his guilty conscience. Late that night, Davy confesses everything to Anne, who forgives him and encourages him to apologize to God.

value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

unit: Anne completes her school term and travels to Charlottetown for the Queen's Academy entrance examinations. label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. label: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
value: Davy questions Anne about sleep.
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. Diana tells Anne about a willow-ware platter at the Copp home on the Tory Road, which they decide to retrieve the following day. When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Anne to the Rescue
unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. unit: Anne and Diana walk along Birch Path on Anne's thirteenth birthday, discussing growing up, school assignments, and romantic story plots. The next day, to Anne's surprise, Anthony shows newfound respect for her, which Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms was earned through the whipping.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

value: Marilla returns to Green Gables.
chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla returns to Green Gables with the orphaned twins, Davy and Dora, whose playful and rowdy behavior immediately poses a challenge for Marilla and Anne. At church on Sunday, Davy creates a commotion by dropping a caterpillar down Lauretta White's neck during the service. Later in the week, Davy ruins Dora's dress by forcing her to walk the pigpen fence and pumps water over her, subsequently confessing to Anne that he also hid a toad in Marilla's bed.

chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

After weeks of anxious waiting, Diana rushes to Green Gables with the published results to reveal that Anne has tied for first place on the Island alongside Gilbert Blythe. Overjoyed, Anne shares the proud news with Matthew, Marilla, and Mrs. Lynde before ending her night with a thankful prayer.

unit: Anne and Diana excitedly prepare a elaborate dinner and floral decorations at Green Gables for a guest, Mrs. Morgan. However, chaos ensues when Davy ruins the lemon pies, the peas are ruined by being oversweetened by too many cooks, and Mrs. Morgan fails to show up. To cap off the disastrous day, Miss Barry's expensive platter is accidentally smashed, and Anne later receives a letter explaining Mrs. Morgan injured her ankle.

unit: Janet takes Anne to a prayer meeting in Valley Road, where they meet John Douglas, who walks Janet home. Anne notices John's pained expression during the visit and wonders about the true dynamic in his household as they return to Wayside.

value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

chapter: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
unit: Anne and Diana travel along the Newbridge road to collect subscriptions for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society to repaint the local hall. They encounter pessimistic Miss Eliza Andrews, who refuses to give anything, though her sister Catherine secretly donates afterwards. Later, Anne recounts to Marilla how they helped flustered Dan Blair mix a cake in exchange for a generous donation, followed by their visit to meticulous Mrs. Theodore White.

label: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
value: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora.
chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora, leaving Anne to do household chores while Davy goes to help Mr. Harrison. While transferring bed feathers, Anne mistakenly applies rug dye to her nose instead of freckle lotion, turning it bright red just before Priscilla Grant arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. Diana helps Anne wash off the dye and supplies a roast chicken, allowing Anne to successfully entertain her visitors with a lovely dinner and a walk through the surrounding woods.

unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

value: Anne returns to Avonlea.

unit: Upon returning to Avonlea, Anne notices small changes in the community and learns from Rachel Lynde that Ruby Gillis is terminally ill with consumption. Anne confides in Diana her ambition to write a short story before they arrive at the lively Gillis home, where Ruby hides her failing health under a façade of gay flirtation.

value: Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession
unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

value: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

unit: Marilla informs Anne that Miss Stacy visited to recommend that she join an advanced class preparing for the Queen's Entrance examination. After the class is organized, Anne navigates the dynamic of studying alongside her peers—including her rival, Gilbert Blythe—while missing Diana, who is not taking the exam.

value: Marilla returns from the oculist.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
unit: Marilla returns from the oculist with news that her failing sight means she cannot read, sew, or manage Green Gables alone, forcing her to consider selling the farm. Anne refuses to let the home be sold and decides to give up her college scholarship to stay at Green Gables and teach locally. Later, Mrs. Lynde informs them that Gilbert Blythe gave up the Avonlea teaching position so Anne could have it, leading Anne to reconcile with Gilbert and look forward to her future with peace and hope.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. Bedridden for seven weeks while her ankle heals, Anne receives many visitors and eagerly anticipates returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

unit: Anne and Diana walk along Birch Path on Anne's thirteenth birthday, discussing growing up, school assignments, and romantic story plots. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

unit: Marilla informs Anne that Miss Stacy visited to recommend that she join an advanced class preparing for the Queen's Entrance examination. value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: During a party at Diana's house, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, where Marilla experiences a deep realization of how much she cares for the girl. label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field while driving back from Carmody.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: While driving back from Carmody, Anne and Diana spot a Jersey cow in Mr. Harrison's wet oat field and chase it into the lane. Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

Believing the cow to be her own mischievous animal, Dolly, an annoyed Anne impetuously sells it on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning home to Green Gables, Anne discovers her real cow still in the milking pen and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow. Horrified by her mistake, Anne packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess to Mr. Harrison.

unit: On the evening before school opens, Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate their teaching methods and views on corporal punishment at a crossroads. Anne then walks back through her favorite spots, avoids Mrs. Lynde's unsolicited advice at Green Gables, and visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule without whipping. The next morning, a nervous Anne is comforted by Marilla as she prepares for her first day as a teacher.

chapter: v2 · VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women
unit: Anne and Diana travel along the Newbridge road to collect subscriptions for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society to repaint the local hall. They encounter pessimistic Miss Eliza Andrews, who refuses to give anything, though her sister Catherine secretly donates afterwards. Later, Anne recounts to Marilla how they helped flustered Dan Blair mix a cake in exchange for a generous donation, followed by their visit to meticulous Mrs. Theodore White.

label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne converses with Mr. Harrison on his porch about Rachel Lynde, Davy's antics, and the Village Improvement Society's hall painting project. Later, Mrs. Lynde discovers that Joshua Pye has accidentally painted the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up in color codes. The Improvers gather at Green Gables in despair over the blunder, but the town's sympathy ultimately turns in their favor against the Pyes.

Upon returning home, they leap into the spare-room bed as a game, unwittingly jumping directly onto Diana's visiting great-aunt, Aunt Josephine. The resulting uproar leaves Miss Barry furious and threatens Diana's music lessons, prompting a remorseful Anne to seek a way to make amends.

unit: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora, leaving Anne to do household chores while Davy goes to help Mr. Harrison. While transferring bed feathers, Anne mistakenly applies rug dye to her nose instead of freckle lotion, turning it bright red just before Priscilla Grant arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. Diana helps Anne wash off the dye and supplies a roast chicken, allowing Anne to successfully entertain her visitors with a lovely dinner and a walk through the surrounding woods.

unit: During an overnight stay, Jane Andrews proposes to Anne on behalf of her shy brother, Billy. Afterward, Anne reflects with a mixture of amusement and disappointment at how unromantic her very first marriage proposal turned out to be.

label: v3 · Chapter XI The Round of Life
value: Anne returns to Avonlea.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XI The Round of Life
unit: Upon returning to Avonlea, Anne notices small changes in the community and learns from Rachel Lynde that Ruby Gillis is terminally ill with consumption. On their way to visit Ruby, Anne and Diana stop by to leave jelly with the sour and critical Aunt Atossa. Anne confides in Diana her ambition to write a short story before they arrive at the lively Gillis home, where Ruby hides her failing health under a façade of gay flirtation.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE
unit: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children after borrowing a dress, making a impression with her lively behavior and strong singing voice. Afterwards, she settles into the manse, refusing to go to school but diligently cleaning and taking on house chores while clashing slightly with Aunt Martha over the cooking. She spends time playing with the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, fascinating and sometimes infuriating them with her stories, talents, and bold personality while secretly fearing Mrs. Wiley's eventual return.

She spends time playing with the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, fascinating and sometimes infuriating them with her stories, talents, and bold personality while secretly fearing Mrs. Wiley's eventual return.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

value: The Meredith children decide to fast all day Sunday.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
unit: The Meredith children decide to fast all day Sunday as a self-imposed punishment for their Good-Conduct Club, but Una faints during the evening church service from lack of food. Doctor Gilbert Blythe revives Una, and Faith explains to her father and Mrs. Clow that the children are raising themselves. Distressed by Faith's words, John Meredith resolves to be a better father to his children, though he realizes he can never marry anyone but Rosemary West.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE
value: Faith becomes terrified in Rainbow Valley.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE
unit: Faith, Carl, and Una become terrified in Rainbow Valley when they mistake Mrs. Stimson—who is crawling on the Bailey garden dyke with white sheets on her shoulders looking for a knitting needle—for the ghost of Henry Warren. Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to Ingleside, where Rosemary West and Susan Baker soothe them. Susan investigates with a pitchfork and returns to explain the embarrassing truth, prompting the children to retreat home in shame.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXXI. CARL DOES PENANCE
value: Jerry decrees punishments for the children's cowardice.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXXI. CARL DOES PENANCE
unit: Jerry decrees punishments for the children's cowardice, sending Carl to sit in the graveyard until midnight. Carl bravely endures the cold, rainy vigil, but falls dangerously ill with double pneumonia as a result. After a grim fight for his life, Carl recovers with the support of the family and community, and the children celebrate his return to health.

value: Una Meredith is determined to make her unhappy father happy.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXXIV. UNA VISITS THE HILL
unit: Determined to make her unhappy father happy, Una Meredith visits her late mother's gray dress in the spare room before walking to the West house to speak with Rosemary West. Thinking stepmothers are cruel, Una selflessly begs Rosemary to marry her father and promises that the children will behave. Rosemary reassures Una, writes a letter agreeing to meet John Meredith, and sends Una back to the manse to deliver it.

value: While their father and Jerry are away, Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXVIII. A FAST DAY
unit: The Meredith children decide to fast all day Sunday as a self-imposed punishment for their Good-Conduct Club, but Una faints during the evening church service from lack of food. Doctor Gilbert Blythe revives Una, and Faith explains to her father and Mrs. Clow that the children are raising themselves. Distressed by Faith's words, John Meredith resolves to be a better father to his children, though he realizes he can never marry anyone but Rosemary West.

value: The Meredith children sit in the old Methodist graveyard.

unit: The Meredith children sit in the old Methodist graveyard chatting about town gossips, buried people, and their new Blythe neighbors. label: v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE
value: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE
unit: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children after borrowing a dress, making a impression with her lively behavior and strong singing voice. Afterwards, she settles into the manse, refusing to go to school but diligently cleaning and taking on house chores while clashing slightly with Aunt Martha over the cooking. She spends time playing with the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, fascinating and sometimes infuriating them with her stories, talents, and bold personality while secretly fearing Mrs. Wiley's eventual return.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to Ingleside, where Rosemary West and Susan Baker soothe them. Susan investigates with a pitchfork and returns to explain the embarrassing truth, prompting the children to retreat home in shame.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

unit: John Meredith becomes engrossed in German theology, forgetting his parish duties and family until the wealthy and overbearing Mrs. Alec Davis visits the manse. Shaken by her accusations, Mr. Meredith reflects on his shortcomings as a father and decides to seek advice from Mrs. Blythe at Ingleside.

unit: Faith is furious with Aunt Martha for killing her rooster, Adam, to feed a visiting minister, Mr. Perry. During Sunday dinner, Faith fumes as Mr. Perry eats Adam and patronizes the family. chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXXIV. UNA VISITS THE HILL
unit: Determined to make her unhappy father happy, Una Meredith visits her late mother's gray dress in the spare room before walking to the West house to speak with Rosemary West. value: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE
unit: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children after borrowing a dress, making a impression with her lively behavior and strong singing voice. Afterwards, she settles into the manse, refusing to go to school but diligently cleaning and taking on house chores while clashing slightly with Aunt Martha over the cooking. She spends time playing with the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, fascinating and sometimes infuriating them with her stories, talents, and bold personality while secretly fearing Mrs. Wiley's eventual return.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE
unit: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children after borrowing a dress, making a impression with her lively behavior and strong singing voice. Afterwards, she settles into the manse, refusing to go to school but diligently cleaning and taking on house chores while clashing slightly with Aunt Martha over the cooking. She spends time playing with the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, fascinating and sometimes infuriating them with her stories, talents, and bold personality while secretly fearing Mrs. Wiley's eventual return.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

unit: Mary Vance visits the manse children in the graveyard to lecture them on their misbehaviour and gossip about their father's potential romance with Rosemary West. label: v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”
value: Faith attends church without stockings.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXV. ANOTHER SCANDAL AND ANOTHER “EXPLANATION”
unit: Faith causes a scandal at church by attending without stockings, which leads to gossip across the Glen and discussions among Anne, Susan, and Miss Cornelia. In Rainbow Valley, Nan and Di defend Faith when Mary Vance criticizes her, but Jerry and the Conduct Club decide to punish Faith by making her wear her hated striped stockings. To clear her father's name and clarify other misunderstandings, Faith writes and publishes a detailed letter of explanation in the local newspaper.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE
unit: Faith, Carl, and Una become terrified in Rainbow Valley when they mistake Mrs. Stimson—who is crawling on the Bailey garden dyke with white sheets on her shoulders looking for a knitting needle—for the ghost of Henry Warren. Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to Ingleside, where Rosemary West and Susan Baker soothe them. Susan investigates with a pitchfork and returns to explain the embarrassing truth, prompting the children to retreat home in shame.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE
unit: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children after borrowing a dress, making a impression with her lively behavior and strong singing voice. chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

unit: Anne joins Marilla, Mrs. Rachel, Dora, and Davy outside on a June evening. Davy complains about his schoolwork and the local funerals, but Anne offers to help him with his arithmetic. The conversation turns to local gossip, including Diana's upcoming wedding to Fred Wright and the town's reaction to Anne rejecting Gilbert Blythe. Anne later wanders down to Dryad's Bubble, feeling melancholic about Gilbert's absence and the changes that growing up brings.

unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

label: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
value: Davy questions Anne about sleep
chapter: v2 · XVIII An Adventure on the Tory Road
unit: Davy questions Anne about sleep and Marilla's frugality before Marilla calls Anne over to see Diana's signal. Diana tells Anne about a willow-ware platter at the Copp home on the Tory Road, which they decide to retrieve the following day. When they arrive at the empty Copp house, Anne climbs onto an old duck house to look through the pantry window, falls through the roof, and gets trapped. After sitting through a rainstorm while stuck, Anne is rescued by Miss Sarah Copp, who agrees to entertain selling her the platter over tea.

unit: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora, leaving Anne to do household chores while Davy goes to help Mr. Harrison. Diana helps Anne wash off the dye and supplies a roast chicken, allowing Anne to successfully entertain her visitors with a lovely dinner and a walk through the surrounding woods.

unit: Anne joins Marilla, Mrs. Rachel, Dora, and Davy outside on a June evening. Davy complains about his schoolwork and the local funerals, but Anne offers to help him with his arithmetic. The conversation turns to local gossip, including Diana's upcoming wedding to Fred Wright and the town's reaction to Anne rejecting Gilbert Blythe. Anne later wanders down to Dryad's Bubble, feeling melancholic about Gilbert's absence and the changes that growing up brings.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE
unit: Faith, Carl, and Una become terrified in Rainbow Valley when they mistake Mrs. Stimson—who is crawling on the Bailey garden dyke with white sheets on her shoulders looking for a knitting needle—for the ghost of Henry Warren. Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to Ingleside, where Rosemary West and Susan Baker soothe them. Susan investigates with a pitchfork and returns to explain the embarrassing truth, prompting the children to retreat home in shame.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE
unit: The children gather in Rainbow Valley to read poems and discuss their future dreams of traveling the world when they grow up. Their tranquil evening is interrupted when Mary Vance arrives and frightens them with the tragic tale of Henry Warren's ghost haunting the nearby Bailey garden. After cooking and eating Jerry's fresh-caught trout, the children disperse for the night, with Faith, Una, and Carl nervously avoiding the old garden on their walk home.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE

unit: After Matthew convinces Marilla to let Anne attend a Debating Club concert and spend the night at Diana's, Anne and Diana enjoy the event together. unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. unit: While Marilla and Mrs. Lynde attend a political rally in Charlottetown, Anne and Matthew spend a quiet evening together studying and talking. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

Diana Barry rushes in to beg for help because her sister Minnie May is gravely ill with croup while their parents are away. Anne hurries to the Barry home and successfully treats Minnie May using her past experience with Mrs. Hammond's children, saving the baby's life. Touched by Anne's rescue, Mrs. Barry forgives her for the past incident with Diana, allowing the two girls to be best friends once again.

unit: Anne and Diana walk along Birch Path on Anne's thirteenth birthday, discussing growing up, school assignments, and romantic story plots. value: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

unit: During an overnight stay, Jane Andrews proposes to Anne on behalf of her shy brother, Billy. chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: Marilla departs Green Gables with Dora, leaving Anne to do household chores while Davy goes to help Mr. Harrison. While transferring bed feathers, Anne mistakenly applies rug dye to her nose instead of freckle lotion, turning it bright red just before Priscilla Grant arrives with famous author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. Diana helps Anne wash off the dye and supplies a roast chicken, allowing Anne to successfully entertain her visitors with a lovely dinner and a walk through the surrounding woods.

value: Anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: After anonymous newspaper notes predict a severe storm, an unusually devastating hailstorm strikes Avonlea, severely damaging crops, trees, and windows. At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

At Green Gables, Anne, Marilla, and the twins shelter through the tempest, later learning that Mr. Harrison's parrot was killed and an eyesore house was struck by lightning. Neighbors assess the ruin, and Uncle Abe basks in his newly acquired fame as a prophet.

label: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
value: Anne finishes term examinations at Redmond College.
chapter: v3 · Chapter VII Home Again
unit: After finishing term examinations at Redmond College, Anne returns home to Green Gables for the Christmas holiday where she is warmly greeted by Diana, Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and the twins. That night, Anne helps a troubled Davy through a dilemma about wanting to say a bad word so that he feels ready to say his prayers. During the break, Anne receives letters from her friends, shares news with her family, and visits Echo Lodge with Diana to air out the house and listen to the echoes once more.

unit: Anne joins Marilla, Mrs. Rachel, Dora, and Davy outside on a June evening. Davy complains about his schoolwork and the local funerals, but Anne offers to help him with his arithmetic. label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

unit: John Meredith becomes engrossed in German theology, forgetting his parish duties and family until the wealthy and overbearing Mrs. Alec Davis visits the manse. Shaken by her accusations, Mr. Meredith reflects on his shortcomings as a father and decides to seek advice from Mrs. Blythe at Ingleside.

unit: Faith is furious with Aunt Martha for killing her rooster, Adam, to feed a visiting minister, Mr. Perry. During Sunday dinner, Faith fumes as Mr. Perry eats Adam and patronizes the family. Distressed by Faith's words, John Meredith resolves to be a better father to his children, though he realizes he can never marry anyone but Rosemary West.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE
value: The children gather in Rainbow Valley.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE
unit: The children gather in Rainbow Valley to read poems and discuss their future dreams of traveling the world when they grow up. Their tranquil evening is interrupted when Mary Vance arrives and frightens them with the tragic tale of Henry Warren's ghost haunting the nearby Bailey garden. After cooking and eating Jerry's fresh-caught trout, the children disperse for the night, with Faith, Una, and Carl nervously avoiding the old garden on their walk home.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE
unit: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children after borrowing a dress, making a impression with her lively behavior and strong singing voice. Afterwards, she settles into the manse, refusing to go to school but diligently cleaning and taking on house chores while clashing slightly with Aunt Martha over the cooking. She spends time playing with the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, fascinating and sometimes infuriating them with her stories, talents, and bold personality while secretly fearing Mrs. Wiley's eventual return.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XV. MORE GOSSIP
unit: Cornelia Bryant, Susan Baker, and Anne discuss the recent funeral of Myra Murray and gossip about local church business and parish families. Mary Vance finishes her knitting and runs down to Rainbow Valley, where she tells Faith Meredith about Mrs. Alec Davis leaving the church and the potential loss of ministry salary. Horrified at the thought of having to move away from Glen St. Mary, Faith decides she must act to convince Norman Douglas to return to the congregation.

Distressed by Faith's words, John Meredith resolves to be a better father to his children, though he realizes he can never marry anyone but Rosemary West.

label: v5 · CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE
value: The children gather in Rainbow Valley.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE
unit: The children gather in Rainbow Valley to read poems and discuss their future dreams of traveling the world when they grow up. Their tranquil evening is interrupted when Mary Vance arrives and frightens them with the tragic tale of Henry Warren's ghost haunting the nearby Bailey garden. After cooking and eating Jerry's fresh-caught trout, the children disperse for the night, with Faith, Una, and Carl nervously avoiding the old garden on their walk home.

Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to Ingleside, where Rosemary West and Susan Baker soothe them. label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

unit: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children after borrowing a dress, making a impression with her lively behavior and strong singing voice. Afterwards, she settles into the manse, refusing to go to school but diligently cleaning and taking on house chores while clashing slightly with Aunt Martha over the cooking. She spends time playing with the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, fascinating and sometimes infuriating them with her stories, talents, and bold personality while secretly fearing Mrs. Wiley's eventual return.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE
unit: Mary Vance attends church with the manse children after borrowing a dress, making a impression with her lively behavior and strong singing voice. Afterwards, she settles into the manse, refusing to go to school but diligently cleaning and taking on house chores while clashing slightly with Aunt Martha over the cooking. She spends time playing with the Meredith and Blythe children in Rainbow Valley, fascinating and sometimes infuriating them with her stories, talents, and bold personality while secretly fearing Mrs. Wiley's eventual return.

unit: The children gather in Rainbow Valley to read poems and discuss their future dreams of traveling the world when they grow up. value: Faith becomes terrified in Rainbow Valley.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE
unit: Faith, Carl, and Una become terrified in Rainbow Valley when they mistake Mrs. Stimson—who is crawling on the Bailey garden dyke with white sheets on her shoulders looking for a knitting needle—for the ghost of Henry Warren. Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to Ingleside, where Rosemary West and Susan Baker soothe them. Susan investigates with a pitchfork and returns to explain the embarrassing truth, prompting the children to retreat home in shame.

chapter: v5 · CHAPTER XXX. THE GHOST ON THE DYKE
unit: Faith, Carl, and Una become terrified in Rainbow Valley when they mistake Mrs. Stimson—who is crawling on the Bailey garden dyke with white sheets on her shoulders looking for a knitting needle—for the ghost of Henry Warren. Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to Ingleside, where Rosemary West and Susan Baker soothe them. Susan investigates with a pitchfork and returns to explain the embarrassing truth, prompting the children to retreat home in shame.

unit: Following Captain Jim's passing and the success of his life book, Gilbert proposes buying the larger Morgan place in the Glen to accommodate their growing family and practice. After packing up and saying an emotional farewell to each room, Anne and Gilbert lock up their house of dreams and depart for the Glen.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid
unit: Anne and her friends reenact Tennyson's Elaine on the pond, but the dory leaks and begins to sink, forcing Anne to cling to a bridge pile. Gilbert Blythe rows by and rescues her, but Anne angrily refuses his offer of apology and friendship. Later, back at Green Gables, Anne reflects on learning her lesson about romance, while Matthew gently advises her not to abandon it entirely.

label: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
value: While their father and Jerry are away, Faith and Una try to manage the household.
chapter: v5 · CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE
unit: While their father and Jerry are away and Aunt Martha is bedridden with an illness, Faith and Una try to manage the household and care for a sick Carl. On Monday, they attempt to clean the house and shake rugs in the adjacent graveyard, inadvertently causing a scandal in the community when neighbors mistake their actions as occurring on Sunday. Despite running low on food and struggling with cooking, their troubles end when Aunt Martha recovers, sunshine returns, and the Blythes come back to join them in Rainbow Valley.

Terrified, the Meredith children sprint to Ingleside, where Rosemary West and Susan Baker soothe them. Susan investigates with a pitchfork and returns to explain the embarrassing truth, prompting the children to retreat home in shame.

Thinking stepmothers are cruel, Una selflessly begs Rosemary to marry her father and promises that the children will behave. Rosemary reassures Una, writes a letter agreeing to meet John Meredith, and sends Una back to the manse to deliver it.
